title: sidecar-fallback-telemetry-bridge-and-softbackpressure
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a sidecar fallback telemetry bridge and opt-in soft backpressure path to reduce SLO breaches during regional KV drain and network blips. No configuration changes for default tenants; opt-in via route flag.
description:
Summary: Implement a lightweight sidecar fallback telemetry bridge plus a soft backpressure path to improve graceful degradation when regional KV/drain or noisy egress causes SLO strain.
Motivation: During a recent incident (linked ENG-4023) we observed repeated tenant-level SLO blips while attempting KV drain and peer failover. The root cause was twofold: 1) requests routed through the fast-path sidecar lost timely circuit state telemetry and 2) the control-plane decision to shed traffic lacked a short-circuit soft backpressure path, forcing abrupt circuit flips.
This PR adds: - a telemetry bridge in the sidecar that mirrors a compact circuit-state summary to the local evictor so decisions can be made locally during transient control-plane lag, - an opt-in soft-backpressure channel that gently reduces admission rate for non-critical tenants (route flag and per-tenant hint), and - metrics and histograms to track bridge lag, replay rate, and soft-backpressure effectiveness.
Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed in Linear (ENG-4023) - [x] Sidecar bridge implementation (Go) - [x] Local enforcer hook and backpressure policy - [x] Unit tests for enforcer and bridge replay logic - [x] Integration test in staging that simulates KV drain and egress blip - [x] Telemetry dashboards (metrics.yaml) - [x] Rollout plan and opt-in gating described in PR notes
Commits (3): 1) add: sidecar telemetry bridge and protobuf message (sidecar/fallback_bridge.go, sidecar/proto/circuit_bridge.proto) 2) modify: local slo enforcer to accept bridged state and trigger soft backpressure hint (pkg/slo/enforcer.go, pkg/slo/policy.go, internal/backpressure/soft.go) 3) tests/docs: unit/integration tests and metrics spec (tests/integration/kv_drain_sim.go, telemetry/metrics.yaml, docs/ops/sidecar-fallback.md)
Files changed (high level): - services/sidecar/fallback_bridge.go: implements compact state mirror, connection pooling to local enforcer, and replay/backoff. - sidecar/proto/circuit_bridge.proto: compact protobuf describing epoch, penalty_score, sticky_until, ttl. - pkg/slo/enforcer.go + pkg/slo/policy.go: accept bridged state with bounded trust window, apply soft backpressure instead of immediate eviction when policy matches. - internal/backpressure/soft.go: new soft backpressure admission controller. - telemetry/metrics.yaml: histograms for bridge-latency_ms, replay_count, soft_backpressure_ratio. - tests/integration/kv_drain_sim.go: staging scenario that toggles KV availability and asserts SLO quantiles. - docs/ops/sidecar-fallback.md: rollout and opt-in instructions.
Review summary: - Diego Ramos: Called out potential trust model for bridged state (how stale can we accept). Suggested bounding by epoch and applying a decay factor. Diego requested an explicit test for epoch-stale rejection. - Author (Maya): Added epoch check and decay factor; extended unit test to include stale epoch case. - Nora Singh: Asked about CPU impact in heavily-loaded sidecars. Response: the bridge uses a p99-sized serialization pool and avoids extra goroutines per request; we added a sampling rate config (default 1%) and a telemetry sampling override for debugging. - Ethan Park: Requested a rollback plan and opt-out flag. Added route-level opt-in flag and operator-level global disable.
Conversation excerpts: - Diego Ramos (2026-02-11): "We need a strict contract for staleness — otherwise local decisions might diverge and cause oscillation." - Maya Patel (2026-02-12): "Added epoch and monotonic penalty decay; stale frames are ignored after 2x configured TTL." - Nora Singh (2026-02-13): "What's the expected CPU delta for sidecars at 1% sampling? Please capture in staging run." - Maya Patel (2026-02-16): "Staging run shows ~0.8% CPU increase at p95 for default sampling; can be tuned via config." - Ethan Park (2026-02-17): "Approve — please monitor the alert thresholds closely during canary." 
CI summary: - unit: pass - integration: initially failed on flakey test (kv_drain_sim) due to race on mock clock; fixed with explicit clock barrier and re-run - e2e/staging: pass (staging harness simulated KV drain across 3 AZs and asserted 99th latency under the soft path)
Risk/rollback: - Opt-in default: the feature is off by default for tenant routes. - Operator rollback: new cluster flag redwood.sidecar.bridge.enabled=false will disable creation of bridge endpoints and revert enforcer trust window to control-plane-only. - Quick rollback plan included in docs/ops/sidecar-fallback.md.
Observability and SLOs: - New metrics added; dashboards attached in telemetry/metrics.yaml and Grafana JSON linked in the doc. - Alerts: added AlertRule SRE_SOFT_BACKPRESSURE_FALLTHROUGH if bridged-replay_rate > 5% and error_ratio increases for 5m.
Rollout plan: 1) Canary enabling on internal org for 24h with aggressive telemetry sampling 2) Monitor replay lag and soft_backpressure_ratio for 48h 3) Gradual opt-in to customers that opt-in via routes 4) Default sampling set to 0% for public tenants until final signoff
Merge outcome: squash-merged to main on 2026-02-24 by Maya Patel after approvals from Diego and Nora (Ethan approved via comment). Notes: This PR was intentionally small in scope to reduce blast radius; two follow-ups are planned: (a) a control-plane companion that aggregates bridge telemetry for long-term trends and (b) automated tuning of sampling based on load and bridge-lag. Related: ENG-4023 (incident), SRE-88 (postmortem action).
